newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Juppe wins lukewarm confidence vote.
newsitem.headline: France's Juppe wins lukewarm confidence vote.

text.p: Embattled French Prime Minister Alain Juppe won a lukewarm vote of confidence from the Senate on Tuesday after reaffirming he wanted to step up the battle for jobs.
Senators voted by 219 to 94 to endorse Juppe in a confidence vote mirroring an unenthusiastic vote last week by the National Assembly, the lower house of parliament.
Juppe's centre-right allies in the Senate voted for him while the mainly Socialists and Communist opposition voted against. There were two abstentions.
Last week, the National Assembly backed Juppe by 464 to 100 after he called the vote in an effort to silence discontent with his austerity policies within the ranks of his coalition.
Juppe would have resigned had he lost in the National Assembly. By contrast, the Senate vote was a symbolic show of unity for Juppe, who came to power in May 1995.
Shown by opinion polls to be among the least popular of modern prime ministers, Juppe said the government would redouble its efforts to stimulate economic growth and create more jobs.
He insisted, however, that he would not put off necessary reforms to try to woo French citizens and win a boost in the opinion polls.
